description.narrative: Enhancing Namibia’s capacity to establish a comprehensive Transparency Framework for Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) of climate actions and report on Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) implementation under the Paris Agreement

sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

comment.narrative:
1. Initial NDC, Initial, Second, Third and Fourth National Communications; and First, Second and Third BURs submitted to UNFCCC Outcome 1
2. Gender is not mainstreamed into MRV processes and there is a lack of capacity on gender among national stakeholders.
Outcome 2
3. Questionnaires for the collection of data are available for GHG emissions and mitigation, but the capacity of data providers to understand and provide best available data is limited.
Outcome 3
4. There are no templates or operational procedures to collect information on support received. Stakeholders do not have the technical capacity to meet information requirements
Outcome 4
5. The GHG emission scenarios are reviewed and GHG emissions projections are updated using the latest GHG emission inventory available as a reference. Additional mitigations actions are assessed, and their feasible impact incorporated into policy scenarios.
6. The methodology to track progress of the NDC is developed considering the information available in the domestic MRV system.
1. 1 Project approved and funding secured for implementation 2. Amount of Resources Mobilised
1. 1 Project document submitted and approval for funding expected by end of the year 2. Resources mobilized to the tune of USD 1,000,000 mobiles to implement CBIT implement
1. Project Inception Workshop 2. Project Implementation Delivery

1. Project inception Workshop held 2. Project Implementation delivery done 3. 1 Virtual training on conducting Vulnerability and Adaptation Assessment (V&A) training from the 21st to the 25th of June 2021 conducted, where V&A working group members took part.

• 100 direct beneficiaries, of whom 50 are women • Updated NDC submitted to the UNFCCC
Outcome 1: At least 2 workshops on gender mainstreaming have been developed under the project. The technical capacity and expertise in gender mainstreaming of the NCCC and working groups per theme and sector is enhanced.
Outcome 2: All data providers are trained to use the questionnaires and templates for providing data to the MRV system in line with 2006 IPCC methodologies.
Outcome 3: All data providers are trained to use the templates for providing data on support to feed the MRV system. The information on support is integrated in the future BTR.

Results for Indicator 1:
• Capacity building has been on-going throughout the project implementation. There has been a deliberate request for stakeholders to nominate more women to attend trainings on the 2006 Inter-governmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) software. Deliberate attempts have been made to increase the number of women and youth to serve on the national GHG, mitigation and Vulnerability and Adaptation (V&A) working groups.
Results for Indicator 2:
• The MRV portal has just been finalized and awaiting testing, official handover to NSA accompanied by the training of various stakeholders. The trainings, handover and deployment of the portal is planned for the remaining two quarters of 2022. A draft Memorandum of Agreements (MoA) was drafted and submitted to legal advisors in the Attorney Generals office for further input and legal advice (provided as evidence). Once the legal content is approved, several MoAs will be drafted for the various data providers.
Results for Indicator 3:
• The final revised and aligned NDC and an accompanying technical report have now been published on the NDC registry website. A validation workshop was held from the 19th to the 20th of May 2022. The revised NDC is currently awaiting high-level validation before being tabled to the Cabinet for approval and eventually submitted to the UNFCCC.
Results for Indicator 4:
• The project aims at improving institutional capacities for enhanced transparency activities. This has been done through developing tracking tools which are being incorporated in the MRV portal, and through training workshops. A total of 25 technical experts from various key stakeholders participated in the training among whom there were 10 women and 15 men.
Outcome 1
Results for Indicator 5:
• A draft Gender mainstreaming document into the NDC is in place (provided as evidence). A gender sensitivity indicators framework has been developed and included in the MRV portal. This activity is also supported also by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH under the Climate Change and Inclusive Use of Natural Resources (CCIU) project. No gender mainstreaming workshop took place during the reporting period.
Results for Indicator 6:
• The capacity building of the NSA, who will be hosting the platform is planned for during quarter 3 of the year 2022. So far no government agency have used the MRV platform because it has just been developed. The first phase of training will only be provided to NSA and MEFT on the use, maintenance and updating. The second phase will include the working groups collecting, entering and updating data onto the software.
Outcome 2
Results for Indictor 7:
• At least 30 data providers and working group members have participated in training courses on the 2006 IPCC guidelines and software, as well as the 2019 refined IPCC guidelines. Details of the dates and workshop reports are given above. A total of 28 lectures and researchers from various academic institutions participated of which 12 were men and 16 women.
Results for Indicator 8:
• The project is on track to achieve this indicator as the Terms of Reference to develop a detailed QA/QC plan are currently being developed. This work will be initiated in Quarter 3 of 2022. The full fledged QA/QC plan will cover all the sectors, which are: Energy, IPPU, Waste and AFOLU.
Outcome 3
Results for Indicator 9:
• An MRV template for support needed and received is yet to be developed, however this work will commerce during quarter 3 and 4 of 2022. Only after the templates are developed will the data providers be trained on the use of the template
Outcome 4
Results for Indicator 10:
• The revised and aligned NDC has been finalised together with an accompanying technical report (provided as evidence). The NDC is currently waiting for the high-level validation before being presented to the Cabinet for approval. The alignment was being done on the initial NDC and the second NDC to ensure they have the same baseline year and take into account the latest GHG inventory and current socio economic situation of the country.
Results for indicator 11:
• Tracking of progress towards the attainment of the NDC targets has been embedded in the MRV portal. Namibia has started to develop a full NDC implementation strategy and an action plan. Namibia has also managed to secure funding for the preparation of its first BTR and NC5
